newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal may sell gold reserves - Economy Minister.
newsitem.headline: Portugal may sell gold reserves - Economy Minister.

text.p: Portugal may sell part of its substantial gold reserves, Economy Minister Augusto Mateus said.
"Portugal, which holds a large proportion of its reserves in gold, had for some years and still has the possibility to sell part of its gold reserves," Mateus told TSF radio.
Local economists told the radio station that Portugal's expected entry to the planned European single currency would reduce its need for gold reserves.

Bank of Portugal governor Antonio De Sousa told Expresso weekly in an interview published on October 6 that Portugal was not planning to sell some of its gold reserves to help it meet convergence criteria for entry to the single currency.
"The Bank of Portugal is not thinking of selling gold at this time," De Sousa said. "There has been no suggestion from the government to this effect."
